title: Moon Run
premise: A neon sci-fi arcade survival game where the player pilots a glowing lunar beacon through vertically separated hazard bands, trying to keep climbing for maximum altitude.
interaction_model: One-button real-time control; tap/click/pointer press or press Space to apply an upward thrust while gravity continuously pulls the player downward.
objective: Survive as long as possible by threading through obstacle gaps without hitting the ceiling, floor, or hazard bands, and achieve the highest altitude score.
progression: Endless score attack progression with steadily increasing scroll speed, continuous altitude gain over time, and bonus score awarded for successfully passing each obstacle set.
theme: Retro-futurist lunar mission with neon HUD styling, glowing sci-fi visuals, mission-control language, and arcade feedback effects.
mood: Arcade-tense, energetic, reactive, and slightly heroic with a polished neon-space presentation.
likely_audience: Players who enjoy short-session arcade score chasers
Fans of Flappy Bird-like obstacle survival games
Mobile and browser players looking for simple one-touch controls
Players attracted to neon sci-fi presentation
confidence_notes: High confidence in the core mechanic: flap/thrust-based endless obstacle threading.
High confidence in the state flow and progression because the full gameplay code is visible in one file.
Moderate confidence in the exact fiction depth; the lunar mission framing appears to be a thematic wrapper rather than a mechanically deep narrative.
recreation_prompt: Create a polished browser arcade game called "Moon Run" that plays like a neon sci-fi Flappy Bird-style endless survival challenge. The player controls a glowing lunar beacon or small mission core that stays near the left side of the screen and is affected by constant gravity; each tap, click, or Space press applies an immediate upward thrust, creating a rhythmic one-button flight pattern. The goal is to survive as long as possible, climb for altitude, and thread through incoming vertical hazard bands made of a top wall and bottom wall with a randomized gap between them. Touching the ceiling, floor, or either hazard wall ends the run instantly. Use a single full-screen canvas for gameplay with layered HUD overlays: a start screen, an in-run altitude display, and a game-over screen with the final altitude and a retry button. Present everything with a glowing retro-futurist lunar theme: deep-space gradients, cyan and violet neon highlights, a subtle moving grid, a bright moon-glow effect, and a luminous trail behind the player showing recent flight history. Make the player feel responsive by rotating the beacon based on vertical velocity, adding jump shake, floating score text or status particles when the player clears hazards, and short feedback cards or banners for launch, scoring, and crash moments. Progression should be endless rather than level-based: altitude increases over time, each cleared obstacle gives a bonus burst of score, and the scroll speed should gradually ramp up to make precision timing harder. Include simple but punchy audio with launch, jump, score, crash, and looping background music. Keep controls mobile-safe and instantly readable, emphasizing fast restart, score chasing, and a clean arcade feel over narrative complexity.
